newsitem.title: USA: Open skies could boost London-Stansted.
newsitem.headline: Open skies could boost London-Stansted.

text.p: The succesful conclusion of an open skies aviation deal between the UK and the U.S. could boost Federal Express Corp's operations at London-Stansted airport, Fedex chairman Frederick Smith said.

"It will not replace our expanding Paris hub and the relationship between the two is likely to be similar to that between our Pacific hub at Subic Bay in the Philippines and the smaller hub in Taiwan," Smith told journalists here on Wednesday.

Smith said one reason why Fedex had decided in the spring 1996 to choose Paris Charles de Gaulle airport as the site for its European hub was that "both the French transport ministry and the Aeroport de Paris (ADP) understood the growing contribution of airfreight to world trade."
The UK, however, had excluded itself because of "its restrictive policies on traffic rights," he added.
Smith said that Fedex revenues this year are expected to be between 11.3 billion and 11.4 billion dollars, with international operations accounting for a little over three billion.
"Europe probably represents 25 to 30 percent of the international figure, " he said.

Last October, Fedex relaunched an intra-European service and as trade liberalisation grows driven by Internet-based electronic trade, the company "hopes to take advantage of demand from European importers and exporters," Smith said.
He also said Fedex has also increased services to Spain from Paris-CDG and is planning a service to Tel Aviv via Greece or Turkey.

Fedex officials said, although the dates are not formally fixed, planning is based on the first flight starting on March 3 from Paris to Basle and then onwards to either Athens or Istanbul for refuelling and possibly picking up additional cargo.
The flight frequencies and exact route still have to finalised, they added.
